text:
incident-bot: paging oncall: HIGH latency spike observed for hosted inference cluster us-west-2 (p99 > 2s) — alert: KV_CACHE_PRESSURE

neil: picking this up

sam: saw it too, p95 jumped to ~800ms, p99 ~2.3s. streaming stalls for some client streams.

jia: adding metrics — I see KV eviction rate up 8x over baseline, prefill queue length exploded. decode workers are underutilized (CPU low) while prefill CPU is pegged. suggests prefill vs decode imbalance.

rachel: any recent deploys to prefill? autoscaler churn?

neil: no deploys in the last hour. autoscaler did one scale-down->up on pool-3 at 2140000500 but that seemed normal.

ops-bot: host-health summary (last 15m): 3 nodes in pool-3 reported OOM-kills for prefill-worker; evictions spiked.

maria-cs: pinging a customer pings team — some users report streaming pauses and long tail responses. severity: degraded UX, not data loss.

sam: quick hypothesis: prefill tasks creating fragmented KV entries causing high eviction churn; prefill fills large prefix caches that conflict with decode cache usage -> eviction thrashing -> tail latency.

jia: supporting data:
```
metric: kv.prefill.queue.length = 120 (baseline 5)
metric: kv.evictions/sec = 480 (baseline 60)
metric: decode.worker.util = 22% (baseline 70%)
metric: stream.stalls/1000 = 45 (baseline 2)
```

neil: ok immediate mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily reduce prefill concurrency 2) widen eviction thresholds (raise max_kv_items) 3) route heavy streaming customers to fallback model (smaller context) 4) scale pool-3 by +2 nodes. Which is lowest-risk first?

rachel: widening eviction threshold is config change but cheap; increases memory usage though. Reducing prefill concurrency is safe and fast (config reload). Scaling nodes is slower but effective.

sam: I can reduce prefill concurrency on pool-3 now. doing: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/prefill-worker PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2`

ops-bot: command executed by sam at 2140001320: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/prefill-worker`

jia: after ~30s I see queue drop from 120 -> 18, evictions/sec down to 120, decode.util climbing back to 55%

maria-cs: any change to customer reports?

neil: still seeing some p99 blips but p95 improving to 420ms. streaming stalls reduced but not gone.

sam: while prefill concurrency is lowering, let's also bump eviction limit temporarily. rachel can you patch configmap kv-cache -> max_items: +20%?

rachel: applying patch now, will roll to pool-3 nodes via daemon. patch:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  max_items: "12000" # was 10000
```

ops-bot: patch applied at 2140001435; cache-daemon rolling restart triggered

jia: after patch evictions/sec ~70, p95 ~300ms, p99 ~900ms, streaming stalls ~8/1000. Looks much better.

neil: good. still need root cause: why did prefill ramp so hard? any bursty traffic?

maria-cs: CS says one large client started a batch of long-context embeddings around 2140000000 that could have flooded prefill. ticket opened with customer.

sam: that matches — long-context requests cause prefill to allocate bigger prefixes; if many concurrent it fragments KV. Also earlier autoscaler scale-down may have left less capacity -> compaction/rehashes.

rachel: we should add a short-term guard: reject or queue long-context prefill beyond X concurrent per-tenant. and re-evaluate prefill task scheduling to prefer decode first when decode backlog > threshold.

neil: agree. action items:
- sam: revert PREFILL_CONCURRENCY to baseline when stable and add per-tenant concurrency guard (Jira INF-3421)
- rachel: monitor memory after eviction bump; if >85% for 10m rollback and instead scale out (Jira INF-3422)
- jia: create P95/P99 waveform graphs and attach epoch of customer long-context requests to correlate (INF-3423)
- maria-cs: follow up with customer and coordinate rate-limited cadence for their batch jobs

sam: I'm going to enable a temporary routing rule: any requests with context > 16k tokens route to a smaller-model variant for 30m to avoid prefill heavy paths. applying via routing service: `routectl set-rule --tag longctx --model=llm-small --ttl=1800`

ops-bot: route rule applied at 2140001579 by sam

jia: metrics after routing rule: p95 260ms, p99 700ms, stream stalls 3/1000. Throughput steady.

neil: looks stable. logging incident as Sev2 with root-cause suspected: KV cache fragmentation due to concurrent long-context prefill and temporary autoscaler capacity dip.

maria-cs: customers impacted: 7 tenants with >0.5% streaming stall complaints. none reported data loss; all functional after mitigation.

rachel: scheduling a follow-up postmortem window at 2140005000 — let's include infra, runtime, and cs. I'll create draft notes.

sam: final immediate steps: keep prefill concurrency low for 15m, keep routing rule for 30m, watch memory.

neil: thanks team. will handoff to next oncall in 30m — if anything degrades escalate to incident channel.

incident-bot: handoff reminder — oncall transition at 2140002999 (neil -> jia).

neil: dropping final note: observed fragmentation pattern looks like many small prefills touching different kv shards rather than long contiguous prefixes; possible improvement: prefill packing to aggregate prefixes per-request. add to backlog.

maria-cs: patch customer communications now.

sam: closing thread for active mitigation; will reopen if p99 crosses 1s again. :thumbsup:
